slides.heading: Title
slides.text: From Peking University and Google, CITransNet is a context-integrated transformer for auction design. It maximizes seller revenue while staying incentive-compatible, discovers asymmetric solutions, and generalizes to auction sizes it never saw during training.

slides.text: A classic problem in auction theory is designing a mechanism that maximizes the seller's revenue while staying incentive-compatible. Myerson solved the single-item case in 1981, but the multi-item case remains open, and prior deep methods assume fixed or symmetric auctions.

slides.heading: Method
slides.text: CITransNet takes three inputs: the bidding profile, bidder-contexts, and item-contexts. It embeds contexts with bids into a representation per bidder-item pair, then passes it through transformer interaction layers that mix a global average with row and column transformers, staying permutation-equivariant. A final layer outputs allocations and payments, with zero-regret enforced during training.

slides.heading: Key Result
slides.text: Results come in two parts. On single-item settings, CITransNet nearly recovers Myerson's optimal revenue, 0.593 against 0.594, with regret below one thousandth, while context-blind baselines fall short. On the harder multi-item settings, it beats the Item-wise Myerson baseline in all six configurations, with gains reaching ten percent.
